name: Seine
author: E. T. Carter
description: A drift-net billowing in a slow current: a square mesh of cords spans the whole frame, each knot tied to its grid neighbours, while a rolling flow field pushes the net into sagging swells - it bellies toward you and falls away, the near folds brightening as the far ones sink into shadow. The topology is fixed, a true net rather than chance proximity, so it always reads as one continuous web drifting underwater.

params.label: Mesh spacing
params.effect: Spacing of the net knots in CSS px; small weaves a fine tight mesh, large opens it into a coarse net.

params.label: Billow
params.effect: How far the cords swell off their rest grid; 0 holds a flat taut net, high throws it into deep sagging folds.

params.label: Current
params.effect: Speed of the current rolling through the net; 0 freezes the drift, higher sends the swells travelling steadily across it.

params.label: Depth swing
params.effect: How much brighter the near folds are than the far ones; 0 lights the net evenly flat, high sinks the far swells into shadow for a strong depth read.

params.label: Cord weight
params.effect: Half-width of each cord in CSS px; thin reads as fine net twine, thick as soft glowing rope.

params.label: Hue spread
params.effect: How far the palette ranges across the net; low washes it one hue, high cycles colours across the mesh.

params.label: Glow
params.effect: Strength of the soft halo around each cord; low keeps crisp twine, high blooms the net into soft luminous mesh.
